name: Serendipity Arts Festival
funding: Non-profit Serendipity Arts Foundation, founded by Hero Enterprise chair Sunil Kant Munjal. 2025 partners include the Goa government, Hero Insurance Broking, Hero Realty, Campa, Milton and foreign cultural institutes.
watch: On 18 December 2019 the organisers shut two exhibits with CAA and NRC content, citing technical issues. Poets called it political suppression.
why_flagged: Non-profit Serendipity Arts Foundation, founded by Hero Enterprise chair Sunil Kant Munjal. 2025 partners include the Goa government, Hero Insurance Broking, Hero Realty, Campa, Milton and foreign cultural institutes.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts or full trustee list; its patrons page names nine patrons undated, and the 2025 festival partners page shows only logos.

name: Serralves Foundation
records_note: Serralves posts yearly reports with audited accounts from 1989 to 2020 and names founders, but its directors are not named on the governing bodies page.

name: SFMOMA
watch: In 2001, while David A. Ross was director, SFMOMA acquired a 20% interest in John F. Simon Jr.'s ComplexCity (2000), recorded as a "fractional and promised gift of Jeffrey Epstein". In 2009 director Neal Benezra wrote to thank Epstein for his "continued support".
why_flagged: Foundation and government list (June 2025): Ford, Warhol, Luce, Haas, Hearst, Koret and Osher foundations, Grants for the Arts, NEA and IMLS. No corporate sponsor list published.
records_note: Annual reports on its site run 2011 to 2018; Form 990s and audits are on ProPublica, foundation funders are named (June 2025) and trustees listed.

name: Shanghai Biennale
funding: Run by the state-owned Power Station of Art; budget undisclosed and paid mainly from Shanghai city government funds. 2025 partners: Aesop, Denza, Langham hotels and lighting maker Flos.
watch: In 2012 officials demanded cuts to Yuri Albert's work, so he withdrew; a committee rejected Barbad Golshiri's proposal. Both artists published their accounts.
why_flagged: Run by the state-owned Power Station of Art; budget undisclosed and paid mainly from Shanghai city government funds. 2025 partners: Aesop, Denza, Langham hotels and lighting maker Flos.
records_note: The organiser's site renders by script and showed no text, so nothing was checked; the budget is undisclosed and mainly city funds per press.

name: Sharjah Art Foundation
watch: Gulf state body; 2011 censorship and director's sacking.
why_flagged: Gulf state body; 2011 censorship and director's sacking.
records_note: Its site has no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board list; the sponsors page names no one.

name: Sinchon Museum of American War Atrocities
watch: Rebuilt on a new site in July 2015. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: Memorial to the 1950 Sinchon massacre. The museum claims over 35,000 deaths and blames US forces; South Korean research finds anti-communist vigilantes and secret police carried out killings.
records_note: A North Korean state museum; no official website, report, accounts, donor list or board turned up.

name: Slovak National Gallery
funding: State gallery funded by Slovakia's Ministry of Culture. Its 2025 budget of €13.2M was later cut to €9.6M; admission revenue was about €330,700.
watch: Šimkovičová dismissed director Alexandra Kusá in August 2024 and accused her of a conflict of interest, which Kusá denies. Rallies and a 360-signature letter followed.
why_flagged: State gallery funded by Slovakia's Ministry of Culture. Its 2025 budget of €13.2M was later cut to €9.6M; admission revenue was about €330,700. No corporate sponsor list found.
records_note: Reports of activity and economy run from 2001 to 2025 and accounts are in the Slovak register; no sponsor list or gallery council is posted.

name: Smithsonian, Air and Space
watch: Boeing, Northrop Grumman and Lockheed name galleries; Koch hall kept.
why_flagged: Boeing, Northrop Grumman and Lockheed name galleries; Koch hall kept.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2016 to 2025, a named donor page and a board; the Smithsonian posts audited accounts for 2017 to 2025.

name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
funding: $72M annual operating budget. Admissions, Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation endowment, Lavazza, BMW Group cultural partnerships.
watch: Refused Sackler gifts 2019, removed the name 2022.
why_flagged: Refused Sackler gifts 2019, removed the name 2022.
records_note: It posts audited statements (2010, 2020, 2021) and Form 990s for 2017 to 2020 on its site; the Form 990s list the trustees.

name: Sónar Festival
funding: Owned by Superstruct Entertainment, which KKR acquired in 2024. Its site shows the Generalitat, Estrella Damm and drinks brands. Sónar says it sends KKR no money. No budget found.
watch: In June 2025 at least 34 acts, including Arca and Rone, withdrew over KKR's Israel investments and its stake in Sónar's owner.
why_flagged: Owned by Superstruct Entertainment, which KKR acquired in 2024. Its site shows the Generalitat, Estrella Damm and drinks brands. Sónar says it sends KKR no money. No budget found.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts or board; the site footer shows partner logos, undated, including Estrella Damm, Fritz-kola, the Generalitat and Barcelona City Council.

name: SONGEUN
watch: Founder's company is a coal miner and trader.
why_flagged: Founder's company is a coal miner and trader.
records_note: The foundation posts yearly donation disclosures for 2022 to 2025, with a 2024 audit report, but no annual report, donor list or board.

name: Speed Art Museum
watch: Churchill Downs gambling and three spirits firms on roster.
why_flagged: Churchill Downs gambling and three spirits firms on roster.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2016 to 2023, financial reports and Form 990s on its site, names corporate supporters undated, and lists its trustees.
